_note: Risk handling (#220). `substitutes` maps an ingredient id to what to use when the shop is out of it; null marks an ingredient with no good substitute, so it is worth buying first. General cooking guidance, not tested against these exact recipes; the id list is checked against the catalogue by a test. Ingredients with no entry are never flagged.

substitutes.chicken-thigh: chicken breast, cut thicker and cooked a little less
substitutes.beef-mince: pork or lamb mince, same cooking time
substitutes.beef-rump: sirloin or scotch fillet, sliced the same way
substitutes.pork-mince: chicken mince, cooked until no pink remains
substitutes.pork-belly: pork shoulder, simmered a little longer until tender
substitutes.pork-loin-chop: pork cutlets or chicken thigh fillets
substitutes.natural-yoghurt: Greek yoghurt loosened with a splash of water
substitutes.cream: coconut cream, which adds a mild coconut flavour
substitutes.lemongrass: lemongrass paste (1 tsp a stalk) or lime zest
substitutes.fish-sauce: soy sauce with a squeeze of lime
substitutes.oyster-sauce: hoisin sauce, or soy sauce with a pinch of sugar
substitutes.hoisin-sauce: oyster sauce with a pinch of sugar
substitutes.fresh-coriander: parsley or the green tops of spring onions
substitutes.ginger: ground ginger, a quarter of the amount
substitutes.water-chestnuts: diced celery or cucumber for the crunch
